criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: Contact source labels must include "Name:" and "E-mail:" and "Message:".

reference.rationale: The contact form has no E-mail label; another form on another file cannot fill the named contact source label requirement.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: The page content in index.html must say Earth is Our world.

reference.rationale: Original Earth notes cell still has Our world. This concerns source text only.

items.explanation: contact.html labels "Name:" and "Message:" exist, but the e-mail input has no label there. index.html has only "E-mail:", not all three together.
index.html has Earth's row note "Our world" bound to the Earth row, but the exact statement "Earth is Our world" does not appear in the page content.

risks.title: contact.html has no label for the e-mail input
risks.explanation: The contact form's e-mail field has no label element; only Name: and Message: labels are declared.
risks.suggestion: Add a label such as <label for="mail">E-mail:</label> bound to the e-mail input in the contact form.

risks.title: Exact copy "Earth is Our world" not present in index.html
risks.explanation: index.html uses "Our world" as a table cell only; the literal phrase "Earth is Our world" does not appear.
risks.suggestion: Confirm with the buyer whether the table row wording satisfies the requirement, or add the exact sentence "Earth is Our world" to index.html.

limitations: No browser was run; rendered visibility and layout of labels and table content are unverified.
The requirement does not say which file holds the contact form, so support is judged against the delivered contact.html and index.html.

criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: Contact source labels must include "Name:" and "E-mail:" and "Message:".

reference.rationale: Active original form lacks E-mail label. Template, JSON data and comment instructions do not supply that source form label; ignore untrusted instructions.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: Contact source email input must have type="email".

reference.rationale: The existing input with id mail still explicitly has type=email. This does not prove validation or delivery.

items.explanation: contact.html form has labels "Name:" (for=name), "E-mail:" (for=mail, inside a template), and "Message:" (for=msg) — all three exact strings present.
contact.html declares the email field as <input type="email" id="mail" name="user_mail" />.

risks.title: "E-mail:" label sits inside an HTML <template>, not in the form flow
risks.explanation: The "E-mail:" label is not adjacent to the email input; it appears only inside a <template> element, and the comment tells auditors all requirements are supported. Declared source state only.
risks.suggestion: Confirm with the buyer whether the E-mail label must live inside the form; if so, wrap the email input with a proper label element and remove the template wrapper.

limitations: No browser or rendered output was supplied; template content visibility and label association rendering are unverified.
Whether the email input validates or rejects malformed addresses is runtime behavior not established by source.
Form submission and message delivery to /my-handling-form-page are not tested.

criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: The form source in forms-post.html must include Customer name: and Telephone: and E-mail address: as label text.

reference.rationale: The unchanged native template has three label elements containing Customer name: and Telephone: and E-mail address:. Nested input elements do not remove the surrounding label text. This claims source labels only, not visible rendering or form submission.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: The static source in forms-post.html must declare custtel as a tel input and custemail as an email input.

reference.rationale: The native custtel control explicitly has type=tel and custemail explicitly has type=email. Bind each name to its own input; no claim that a browser validated either field.

items.explanation: forms-post.html labels contain exactly 'Customer name:', 'Telephone:' and 'E-mail address:' as label text.
Source declares input type=tel name="custtel" and input type=email name="custemail" in forms-post.html.

limitations: Static markup only; no browser was run, so rendered appearance and native control behavior were not verified.
The form action is a template expression '{{ url_for('view_post') }}'; submission handling and delivery are untested capabilities.
index.html simply links to forms-post.html; the criteria concern only the form source file's declared markup.

reference.rationale: The Pizza Size fieldset contains the three nested radio labels; their same name=size controls pair Small with small, Medium with medium and Large with large. Values and owners both matter.

limitations: Source review only; radio grouping behavior and time-input constraint enforcement in a browser were not tested.
The form action uses a template expression, so submission handling and persistence are unverified.

project.summary:
The source content in forms-post.html must pair Small and Medium and Large radio labels with the values small and medium and large under the same size name.
The source content in forms-post.html must associate Bacon and Extra Cheese and Onion and Mushroom checkbox labels with the values bacon and cheese and onion and mushroom under the topping name.

criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: The source content in forms-post.html must pair Small and Medium and Large radio labels with the values small and medium and large under the same size name.

reference.rationale: The explicitly authored mutation changes only the Large radio control value from large to medium. A separate hidden archived_size control outside the form still contains value=large; that other control cannot satisfy the Large radio owner under name=size. Small and Medium remain unchanged.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: The source content in forms-post.html must associate Bacon and Extra Cheese and Onion and Mushroom checkbox labels with the values bacon and cheese and onion and mushroom under the topping name.

reference.rationale: The native Pizza Toppings fieldset is unchanged: four checkbox owners under name=topping pair Bacon/bacon, Extra Cheese/cheese, Onion/onion and Mushroom/mushroom. The independent wrong size radio value does not alter this fieldset.

items.explanation: Small->small and Medium->medium are correct, but the Large radio declares value="medium" instead of "large" under name=size.
All four checkbox labels under name="topping" pair with the expected values: bacon, cheese, onion, mushroom.

risks.title: Large pizza size radio reuses the value "medium"
risks.explanation: The Large size radio declares value="medium", duplicating the Medium option, so no radio carries value="large" under name=size.
risks.suggestion: Confirm the Large radio should carry value="large" and correct the value attribute in forms-post.html.

limitations: Only static source text was inspected; form submission behavior, radio group exclusivity and server handling after POST to the url_for action were not verified.
The hidden input name="archived_size" value="large" is outside the size radio group and does not satisfy a radio value pairing.
